title: Outlook: right-click to customise the classic ribbon in new Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the web
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates, user customisation steps and licensing match Microsoft's sources, and searches confirmed the documented gaps in administrator controls. The statement that customisation takes no action on mail should be narrowed to what Microsoft's notice actually describes.

claims.quote: You can now customize the classic ribbon in New Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the Web by right-clicking the ribbon

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Scope: Configuration; controls[0].note; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Ribbon customisation is user-opt-in: users choose to change their own ribbon rather than having a customised layout imposed.
claims.quote: Users can customize the classic ribbon by right-clicking on the ribbon, selecting which commands and groups to display on the Home and View tabs, and arranging them as desired.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and controls[0].api; Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: No administrator role, UI or automation is documented to disable this customisation, prevent users hiding groups, or deploy or lock a ribbon layout.
claims.quote: Searched: 'new Outlook Windows web ribbon customization disable admin Cloud Policy Set-OwaMailboxPolicy ribbon layout'. Opened policy-management, map-classic-outlook-policies-to-new-outlook, EAC policy properties and Set-OwaMailboxPolicy; found no ribbon setting or parameter.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap and notice describe ribbon commands and groups without identifying new data access.
claims.quote: Users can then choose which commands and groups appear on the Home and View tabs and arrange them in their preferred order.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: New Outlook release notes say the Share to Teams button is hidden from the ribbon and menu when the administrator disables that feature.
claims.quote: The Share to Teams button is now hidden from the ribbon and menu when your admin has disabled this feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether the customisation menu respects administrator policies for every command.
claims.quote: Searched: 'new Outlook ribbon Customize Home View reset layout policy disabled commands'. Read new Outlook policy management and searched release notes for ribbon/customiz: Share to Teams hiding is documented, but interaction with this customisation menu is not.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The feature takes no action on mail.
claims.quote: Searched: '"new Outlook" "ribbon" "customization" "mail" data access'. Read the roadmap, MC1485120 and new Outlook release notes; search results describe VSTO ribbon actions, not this feature. No text explicitly states this no-action guarantee.
claims.fix: Replace 'No change: the feature rearranges commands and takes no action on mail.' with 'The roadmap item and MC1485120 describe choosing and rearranging the commands and groups displayed on the Home and View tabs.'

claims.quote: To use the Outlook for Windows desktop app (either the classic or new version) with a Microsoft 365 organizational email address, you need to purchase a plan that includes the desktop versions of the Microsoft 365 apps.
